article.title: NFL EDGE Tuesday Evening Brief
article.dek: Thursday night is Colts at Texans, the board still hasn't flipped to Week 11, and the betting splits show the public and the money on opposite sides of the big spread.

items.headline: Lead: Thursday night is Colts at Texans — and the board hasn't flipped to Week 11 yet
paragraphs: Week 11 opens Thursday night with the Indianapolis Colts at the Houston Texans, 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff at NRG Stadium.

But the app's board hasn't flipped to Week 11 yet. We checked at 6:09 p.m. and again at 6:12 p.m., and it still shows last week's games with the lines pulled. No Week 11 cards, no Thursday prices, no picks in the app yet.
That is the board telling you plainly: there is nothing to play in the app tonight. Thursday's numbers will land when the board flips.
items.takeaway: Thursday night is Colts at Texans, but the board is still on Week 10. Nothing to play in the app tonight — the Week 11 numbers come with the flip.

items.headline: Injury news: Maye likely done for the year, and Thursday's teams are banged up
paragraphs: Drake Maye is believed to have suffered a fractured ankle in Sunday's loss to the Lions, and the early word is he is likely done for the season. The Patriots are on bye this week and don't play again until November 29 at the Chargers, so this doesn't change a game this week — but it changes New England's season. Tommy DeVito is next up if Maye isn't ready for Week 12.
Lamar Jackson's thumb injury is likely to sideline him for the rest of the regular season. He lasted one snap after returning from his ankle injury. Jacoby Brissett stays the Ravens starter.

For Thursday night, Houston's second injury report is rough. Running back Woody Marks (concussion) is unlikely to play on the short week. Edge rusher Danielle Hunter (hamstring) and receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) haven't practiced. Running back David Montgomery (groin), receiver Tank Dell (hand and shoulder), and cornerback Kamari Lassiter (wrist) all sat out Tuesday too.

The Colts aren't healthy either. Cornerbacks Sauce Gardner (calf) and Charvarius Ward (knee) missed practice Monday and Tuesday and are trending out for Thursday. The one settled thing in Indy: the team has already announced Daniel Jones as the starter for Thursday night.

Elsewhere: Baker Mayfield is dealing with a foot strain and is questionable for Sunday at Detroit. Geno Smith's ankle tests showed no major injury, but he is questionable for Sunday. Jordan Addison is expected to have surgery on his thumb. Ladd McConkey's back spasms kept him inactive on Monday night.
Final injury reports and game statuses for Thursday come after Wednesday's practice. The inactive lists land about 90 minutes before kickoff on Thursday.
items.takeaway: Maye is likely done for the year and Jackson is likely out for the regular season. For Thursday, Houston is missing pieces on both sides of the ball and the Colts' top two corners are trending out — with Daniel Jones already confirmed as Indy's starter.

items.headline: Thursday weather in Houston: mild, dry, and under a roof anyway
paragraphs: Thursday night in Houston looks quiet. About 68 degrees at kickoff, wind about 4 mph, partly cloudy, rain chance about 10 percent.
And it barely matters for this game: NRG Stadium has a retractable roof. Just the facts — no weather edge here, and no reason to read one into the total.
items.takeaway: Houston on Thursday: about 68 degrees, light wind, low rain chance — and a roof over the field. Weather is a non-factor for Colts at Texans.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: An empty board is an answer, not a problem
paragraphs: All three headline cards are empty tonight: Hit Rate, Balanced, and Value all say no play. That's not the app failing. That's the app saying there is nothing priced yet.

When the board flips to Week 11, Thursday's game gets priced like any other. Hit Rate is the supported pick that looks most likely to win. Balanced is a strong pick without paying too much — a good starting point if you're new to this. Value is the model's plus-EV play. Each card does a different job, and none of them is the wrong one for doing its job.
Until the flip, don't go hunting for a bet the app hasn't priced. The board refreshes every morning and evening. Thursday morning is the next look.
items.takeaway: No cards tonight because the board hasn't flipped. Don't force a bet the app hasn't priced — check again when the board turns to Week 11.

items.headline: Your book already has Thursday's lines — use Check until the board catches up
paragraphs: Your book doesn't wait for the app. The Texans are 12.5-point favorites just about everywhere, with the total at 44.5. The app's board doesn't have those numbers yet, but Check does the same job: tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and gives you a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.

One thing to watch: the board still lists Week 10 quarterbacks, so it hasn't caught Thursday yet. The news says Daniel Jones starts for the Colts and C.J. Stroud for Houston. When the board flips, check that the quarterbacks on the card match what you know — and if a QB change lands after the flip, Check is how you re-price it at your number.
items.takeaway: The board is behind your book tonight. Type your book's Thursday line into Check and let the app give you a verdict on your price — that's what it's for.

items.headline: The public is on the Colts. The money is on the Texans.
paragraphs: Here's the split on Thursday night, from the free DraftKings row on VSiN's betting splits page. On the spread, 62 percent of the bets are on the Colts getting 12.5 points — but only 33 percent of the money is. Flip it around: the Texans laying 12.5 have just 38 percent of the bets and 67 percent of the money.

That's a real disagreement: most tickets on one side, most dollars on the other. And the line has moved with the money. The Texans opened at -10 at DraftKings and now sit at -12.5, and the spread grew at every book tracked. The total hasn't moved at all — still 44.5.
What could it mean? The bigger, price-sensitive money likes Houston; the crowd likes the points. It is not a pick, and it doesn't override the app. It's one more layer to think with.

What price to watch: if you like Houston, the good number is already gone — the Texans were -10 earlier in the week and now cost -12.5, so don't chase the move just because the money made it. If you like the Colts, the points keep growing: +12.5 now, and Thursday's inactives, about 90 minutes before kickoff, could push it further. Watch whether it crosses 13.

How to use it: take whichever side you actually like and run it through Check at your book's price. If the public keeps hammering the favorite's opponent and the dog gets a better price without any new bad team news, you may be looking at the same football opinion for a better price.
items.takeaway: Most bets are on the Colts, most money is on the Texans, and the line moved toward Houston. Use it as context, not a pick — and run your side through Check at your price.

items.headline: The Texans keep getting more expensive
paragraphs: At DraftKings, the Texans opened at -10 and now sit at -12.5. The Colts' moneyline lengthened from +410 to +470 at DraftKings since Monday, and every book tracked lengthened the Colts' price while the Texans' spread grew by one to two points. The total hasn't budged: 44.5 from the open to now.
There is no single headline behind the move — it came with the market across the week, not with one piece of news. The books kept nudging Houston up while the Colts' price drifted out.

The app hasn't caught any of this yet, because the board is still on Week 10 with no Thursday lines at all. Until the board flips, Check is how you price your book's Thursday number — the app runs your line and price back through the model and tells you bet or no-bet.
items.takeaway: Texans -10 to -12.5 at DraftKings, Colts moneyline drifting out at every book, total steady at 44.5. The app hasn't priced Thursday yet — use Check until it does.

items.headline: Tonight's job: get Thursday ready, don't force Tuesday
paragraphs: There are no games tonight and no cards in the app. The useful thing to do now is decide what you'd play on Thursday at your book's number — Colts +12.5, Texans -12.5, the total at 44.5 — and be ready to run it through Check when the board flips.

If you played anything on Monday night and haven't settled it yet, settle it now while the result is fresh. Settlement is manual — the tracker only works if you're honest with yourself. Log the losers too.

Then wait for the flip. Thursday morning is the next board, and Thursday's inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff. A good number at your book plus a Check bet verdict beats a forced bet on a night with nothing priced.
items.takeaway: Nothing to force tonight. Line up your Thursday number, settle Monday night honestly, and let Check price it when the board flips.
